notes: Search snippet of the DOAJ record confirms title, SLAS Technology Aug 2025 (vol 33, 100307, DOI 10.1016/j.slast.2025.100307), BTK pipeline (screening, GSH reactivity, kinact/Ki) on Echo MS+ / ZenoTOF 7600. Peer-reviewed article; authors also include Bajrami and Nemati (SCIEX-affiliated, so vendor-authored); title says 'Cheng et al.' correctly; no performance numbers claimed. Page itself not opened (blocked).

Nature 636:374-379, Dec 2024, DOI, St. Jude, acoustic ejection MS with fragmentation-pattern barcodes and no chromatography all confirmed (first author Maowei Hu, last Daniel Blair). The '384 reactions across six transformations on one plate' figure was not found in any abstract or snippet and must be checked in the full text. Peer-reviewed; reaction screening, not ADME. Published date is 12 Dec 2024 (online 11 Dec), item says 2024-12-01.

Pittcon listing 'Application of Acoustic Ejection MS to Accelerate Small Molecules Discovery Process', Sun 8 Mar 2026 9:10-9:30, and the ADE/OPI/ESI-MS description confirmed via search snippet; Merck's implementation is stated in the listing's own abstract. Speaker not identified and no data; conference abstract only, single source. Summary 'used in discovery-stage work' slightly paraphrases 'implemented to accelerate' small-molecule work.

Published date 2026-11-03 is a placeholder (SCIEX tech notes are undated); real date unknown. Up to 10x vs LC-MS/MS (23 compounds, human and rat microsomes, duplicates) and 60x / 2 s vs 2 min per sample on ZenoTOF 7600 are confirmed on SCIEX pages, but the 160 vs 11 min per 384-well plate figures were not found. The two notes use different LC-MS baselines (2 min/sample vs implied ~25 s), the equivalence data is a small set (6 analytes) and there is no independent validation. Vendor marketing evidence. Title says Echo MS; 60x is Echo MS+.

Fresh clone of sila_python: README commit 9b0ef09 'Change status to Unmaintained' on 2026-09-17 points to gitlab.com/unitelabs/sila2/sila-python; Maintainer field is blank. PyPI JSON confirms sila2 0.14.0 uploaded 2025-12-01 (still latest) and unitelabs-sila 0.14.0 uploaded 2026-11-02.

Fresh clone of sila_base shows annotated tags v1.0 'Official Release 1.0' (2019-10-01), v1.1 (tag 2022-03-17 on a 2022-02-14 commit) and v1.2 'Official Release 1.2' (tag 2026-02-05 on a 2026-02-04 commit). A search found no v1.2 specification document; the standards page still offers Parts A/B v1.1.

sila_base feature_definitions at master (last commit 2026-06-01): the org/silastandard core and instruments features match the summary. Both LabwareTransfer features are MaturityLevel Verified (created Dec 2022, moved to instruments Apr 2023) and CoverController is Draft. No feature in any namespace covers aspirate, dispense, deck, labware or tips.

Clone confirms a BSD-3 licence (Tecan Trading AG), a C#/.NET server plus Python client, a FluentControl requirement, and commands StartFluentInSimulationMode, RunMethod, PauseRun, SetVariableValue and Aspirate/Dispense/GetTips/DropTips. The last commit is 2025-10-31, but that is a packaging update: the repo was first published 2020-06-15, so the 'publishes' framing and published date are wrong.

notes: The README confirms an on-instrument I.DOT SiLA 2 server that supports only client-initiated connections and mDNS _sila._tcp discovery, with C# client samples. The 2026-02-24 date is the latest commit (net8.0 update); the repo and the native server date from 2022-09-14, so this is not new.

The GitLab API returns 19 projects for the unitelabs group (18 in its namespace), none for Hamilton. UniteLabs' STAR/VANTAGE connectors show up only in vendor docs and hub snippets. The title overstates: public community Opentrons SiLA 2 connectors exist (Acceleration Consortium). The SiLA directory also lists a Zeus (Hamilton OEM channel) driver, interface v1.2, probably SiLA 1-style.

notes: crates.io lists sila2-types, -build, -client and -server 0.1.0, created 2026-11-03 22:00 UTC from gitlab.com/SiLA2/sila_rust, which has a v0.1.0 tag. The README and CHANGELOG report 349/349 server and 104/104 client checks on the SiLA interoperability tester 0.10.3. These results are self-reported from CI, not independently reproduced.

The PR page shows 'Add LADS (OPC 30500-1) model, server, client, sample and docs' by marcschier, opened 31 Oct and merged 1 Nov 2026. It adds Opc.Ua.LADS, Opc.Ua.LADS.Server and Opc.Ua.LADS.Client plus a shaking-incubator sample. The OPC reference gives LADS 1.0.0 a publication date of 2023-11-30.

At commit 7779f50 (2026-11-03): discovery.py covers SiLA 1 (NetBIOS + GetDeviceIdentification) and SiLA 2 (mDNS). grpc.py raw-protobuf helpers are used by the ImageXpress Pico backend, and the INHECO SiLA SOAP transport is used by SCILA and the legacy ODTC backend. No SiLA code exists in the liquid-handling or Hamilton modules.

At commit 46545ea (2026-09-26, also the latest commit for this folder on main): labmcp-sila2 0.1.2 pins sila2>=0.12,<0.15. Its README status reads 'simulated: tested against a real in-process SiLA 2 server (sila2 library ...), not yet verified against vendor servers', and it validates parameters against the FDL.
